$comment: #EXP-1683 ATTACHMENT LINES: the server never appends to a sealed body, so the WRITER names a send's attachments inside the text before sealing (`withAttachmentEmbeds`, `attachmentEmbedCases`, the server's claimAttachments rule): one line per id (once each, in order) the text does not reference yet, a blank line apart, `![name](/api/attachments/<id>)` for an inline image type (`inlineImageTypes`, exact match) and `[name](/api/attachments/<id>)` for anything else, `[` and `]` dropped from the name. So a PDF in a sealed chat is a file row, never a broken image. An upload this process did not record is an image named `image` (the older clients' reading of a bare id). An attachment-only send has no text and is not sealed: the server writes its lines. EXP-1458 (design #EXP-1457): sealed session content, the ONE wire format every platform reads and writes. Replayed x4 through each platform's reference: TS packages/domain-contract/src/sealed-content.ts, Rust enet-core sealed.rs (exported as free functions by exponential-net-ffi, full AND push-only build, and by exponential-net-wasm), Swift + Kotlin through the UniFFI binding. PRIMITIVE: `push_seal(recipient_x25519_public, plaintext)` from enet-core push.rs, byte-exact (fixtures/push-seal.json); secrets are lowercase hex here, everything that travels (public keys, wrapped keys, envelopes) is base64url WITHOUT padding, canonical (a padded, non-alphabet or non-zero-trailing-bits encoding is malformed). TREE KEY: one X25519 keypair per session tree (root) and EPOCH (1-based, <= 2147483647). The ROOT row carries `sessions.seal_public_key` (base64url of 32 bytes, 43 chars) and `sessions.seal_epoch` (int, the current epoch); both NULL until a key exists. `session_keys(root_id, epoch, install_id, wrapped, created_by_install_id, created_at)`, unique (root_id, epoch, install_id): `wrapped` = base64url(push_seal(installs.x25519_public, tree_secret[32])) = 81 bytes. `generateTreeKey()` = 32 random secret bytes + their clamped X25519 public; `wrapTreeKey(installPublic, treeSecret)` / `unwrapTreeKey(installSecret, wrapped)` (fails unless it opens to exactly 32 bytes). READERS of a tree (the server computes them, tRPC sessionKeys): every non-revoked install of the root's starter (`sessions.user_id`) while a member of the root's team; every non-revoked install of every team member when the root is `shared`; the non-revoked installs bound (`installs.device_id`) to the HOST devices row (lib/sessions/host.ts: the starter's own row for the session's `device_id`, else the first row sharing the team) of ANY session in the tree, while its host is a member of the root's team or of that session's team (#EXP-1984: an Assistant's tree roots in its member's personal team, whose one member is its owner, and its children run in the teams of its scope, eagent tree.json `treeTeams`). Nothing else crosses teams. BODY ENVELOPE (`messages.body`, `sessions.sealed_title`, text): `exp-sealed:v1:<epoch>:<b64url push_seal(tree_public, utf8(text))>`. A body without the `exp-sealed:` prefix is plaintext and stays legal (server lines, older rows). Parse: after the prefix, the version runs to the next `:` (or the end); a version other than `v1` = `unsupported` (never an error, never shown as text); for v1 the epoch is decimal without leading zeros, 1..2147483647, then `:` and the payload, which must decode to at least the 49-byte seal overhead; anything else = `malformed`. Open (`openBody(body, keys by epoch)`) gives exactly one status: `plain` (text = the body), `opened` (epoch, text), `noKey` (epoch: this install holds no secret for that epoch yet: show a locked placeholder and wait for the wrap), `unsupported`, `malformed`, `refused` (epoch: the secret did not authenticate it, or the plaintext is not UTF-8). CARD ENVELOPE (`messages.card`, jsonb): `{...clear, "sealed": "v1:<epoch>:<b64url push_seal(tree_public, utf8(JSON(full card)))>"}` (the same sealed-value grammar as the body after its prefix). CLEAR fields (`cardClearFields`): `kind` plus only what routing needs: messageId, sessionId, issueId, pullRequestId, event, status, final, decision, fresh, answered, pictures, story; each is copied from the full card when set (null/absent = omitted) except `answered`, which is `true` when the card carries `answer` or `answers` (or `answered: true`) and absent otherwise, and `pictures` (addendum 2026-10-30: the attachments a card shows, so the server can claim them and build the PR's attachment list), which is PROJECTED: each entry becomes `{label, attachmentId}` with each only when a string (captions, sizes and everything else stay sealed), entries naming neither dropped, omitted when none is left. Addendum 4 (2026-10-30): an entry with a label and no attachmentId is a picture STILL TO UPLOAD: the server mints its upload (`exponential_show`'s curls) and, when it lands, files it on that CLEAR entry only (`{label, attachmentId}`), never touching `sealed`. Addendum 5 (2026-10-30): `story` (the older name of the results flag, false = chat only) stays in clear, copied only when a boolean (absent otherwise), so the server builds PR pictures from a sealed card without opening it: a sealed card's PR pictures (the PR body and `pr open`'s per-platform picture gate) are its CLEAR `pictures` entries that carry an attachmentId, the label standing in for the caption (captions stay sealed: a PR body is a public export and never carries sealed text), none when the clear `story` is false. EVERYTHING else (question, options, plan, questions, picture captions/sizes, surface, summary, answers, title, caption, items, text, headSha...) exists only inside `sealed`, and the sealed JSON is the FULL card (the clear fields included). `splitCard(card)` = {clear, plaintext}; `card.splits` lists EVERY MessageCard kind (packages/db-schema domain.ts) with its clear part, its plaintext and its envelope. The plaintext's key order and whitespace are NOT part of the contract (readers parse it); the vectors are written with sorted keys and no whitespace so sorting serializers (serde_json, JSONSerialization .sortedKeys) reproduce `plaintext` and `envelope` byte-exact, and every platform must at least open every envelope to `card`. Answering re-seals the FULL card with the answers and sets the clear `decision` / `answered`. `openCard(card, keys)`: no `sealed` field = `plain` (the card as is); `sealed` not a string = `malformed`; otherwise the body statuses; `opened` = the sealed card with the clear fields (except the `pictures` projection: the sealed pictures stay whole, except that a sealed picture WITHOUT an attachmentId takes the attachmentId of the first clear entry with its label and, on a plan, every `](upload:<label>)` embed then points at `/api/attachments/<id>`; a sealed attachmentId is never replaced) laid OVER it (the server may update clear flags such as `decision: superseded` without re-sealing); a sealed card whose `kind` differs from the clear `kind`, or that is not a JSON object, = `refused`; any status but plain/opened returns the clear part alone (show the kind's locked placeholder). ESCALATED ASK (addendum 2026-10-30): an `ask` mirror stays clear `{kind: ask, sessionId, messageId}` (its routing); escalating a sealed card into another tree adds `sealedCard` = that card's envelope sealed to the TARGET tree (`sessions.escalateTarget` -> rootId, then `publicKeys`), opened with `openCard` under that tree's keys. SEALED TITLE: `sessions.sealed_title` = a body envelope; the plaintext `title` stays a neutral fallback. KEY API (tRPC `sessionKeys`, authed; the caller must own the `installId` it names, not revoked): `create {rootId, installId, epoch, publicKey, wraps:[{installId, wrapped}]}` (epoch 1 when the root has no key, or `seal_epoch + 1` by the root's starter or an install of the executing device, and by any reader while the root is due for rotation (`rotation`); the caller's install must be a reader and must be among the wraps; every wrap targets a reader); `mine {installId, rootIds?}` -> [{rootId, epoch, wrapped}]; `pending {installId, limit<=200}` -> [{rootId, epoch, publicKey, targetInstallId, targetX25519Public}] = readers without a wrap for the current epoch on roots where installId holds the current epoch (and is still a reader); automatic, no approval; `wrap {installId, wraps:[{rootId, epoch, targetInstallId, wrapped}]}` only for pairs `pending` lists (a pair another holder wrapped meanwhile is skipped); `publicKeys {rootIds}` -> [{rootId, epoch, publicKey}] for keyed roots the caller may read or send to (keyless or invisible roots are omitted). `due {installId, limit<=200}` -> [{rootId, epoch}] = the roots a holder rotates (`rotation`). VECTORS: `tree` (epoch 1) and `rotatedTree` (epoch 2) = fixed secrets and their public keys; `install` = an install's X25519 secret and public; `wrap` = wrapping `wrap.treeSecret` for `wrap.installPublic` with the fixed `wrap.ephemeralSecret` gives exactly `wrapped`, which unwraps with `install.secret`; `body` = sealing `body.text` with `body.ephemeralSecret` (test code only; production draws a fresh ephemeral per seal) gives exactly `body.envelope`; `card.splits` = per kind, `card` splits into `clear` + `plaintext` and seals (with `card.ephemeralSecret`, epoch 1) to exactly `envelope`; `bodyCases` / `cardCases` open with `keys` (epoch -> tree secret hex) to the given status, epoch and text / card. ANSWER CASES (`answerCases`, EXP-1486): which wire a person's `sessions.answer` takes is decided by the STORED card alone, never by whether the tree or this install has a key: a card WITHOUT `sealed` is answered in clear (answer / answers / decision / fresh / feedback as given), even inside a keyed tree (an older row: since #EDE-97 a keyed tree refuses plaintext cards); a card WITH `sealed` that this install opened is answered with `sealedCard` = the opened card answered (card-answer.ts `answeredCard`) and re-sealed to the tree's current key, beside only the clear `decision` / `fresh`; a sealed card this install cannot open (`noKey`, or no current key) is REFUSED locally, no request leaves (a plaintext answer would leak). Each case: `stored` (the card as synced: inline, or `split` = a `card.splits` name whose `envelope` it is), `keys` (`tree` = this install holds `tree`'s key and the tree's current key, `none` = no key at all), `input` (the answer as the card's UI builds it), `wire` (`clear` | `sealed` | `refused`); a `sealed` case lists `clear` (the sealedCard's clear fields) and `opened` (a subset of the opened answered card); `server` = the card the server stamps (card-answer.ts `answeredCard(stored, wire)`, a subset), every non-refused case is accepted. SEALED BY DEFAULT (#EDE-97, the `clearTree` section is its spec): every chat tree is sealed; the one exception is a tree an OUTSIDE MCP client started (`clearTree`).

placeholder.$comment: EXP-1459 (owner: the web slice designs it, iOS/Android/desktop copy it): the ONE locked state x4, for content this install cannot open (yet). A message whose body or card does not open (openBody/openCard status noKey, unsupported, malformed or refused) is LOCKED with a reason: `noKey` = waiting for a holder to wrap the tree key for this install (it opens by itself once `sessionKeys.mine` has the wrap, no reload); `unreadable` = unsupported, malformed or refused (it never opens here). TRANSCRIPT (buildSessionChat, both layouts): a locked message is ONE `locked` row {id, reason, author} at its place, whatever its card kind, painted as THE transcript pill (chats.json TranscriptDivider: centred glass pill, muted xs) with the `icon` concept and `copy[reason]`, never a bubble or a card, no time. A locked waiting question/plan stays out of the dock (it cannot be answered here). CHAT LIST (chatPreview): a locked message counts like any other preview candidate; when it is the one the preview shows (the newest, or the waiting card while needsYou) the preview = {kind: `locked`, text: copy[reason]} painted ITALIC muted like `working`. TITLES: `sessions.sealed_title` that opens = the title; one that does not open falls back to the plaintext `title` (neutral) and the usual derivation (a locked first prompt counts as no prompt). A plaintext body (no envelope) is never locked. CASES: `messageCases` = openMessage({body, card}, keys) -> {locked, body, card} (locked = the reason or null; body empty and card = its clear part when locked); `rowCases` = buildSessionChat's row for a locked message of the root (session-chat.json input shape); `previewCases` = chatPreview over messages already opened.

coldStart.$comment: COLD START (addendum 2026-11-03, Danny's 'Waiting for the key' on every launch): an install's UNWRAPPED tree secrets persist in its secure store (desktop/CLI: the 0600 keyring beside the eNet identity; iOS: the Keychain; Android: the Keystore-sealed vault; web: IndexedDB under a non-extractable AES-GCM key), never on the server, and are loaded into the reader BEFORE the first sealed row renders. Loading is NEVER gated on the network: not on the install's registration, the eNet node, the key holder or `sessionKeys.mine`; the holder, once it runs, uses that SAME key set. A row shown locked (`noKey`) re-opens by itself the moment its key arrives (no sync change, no send needed). A key still missing at launch is fetched by the holder's first pass (a full `mine`), not on send. Each case: `persisted` (epoch -> tree secret hex the previous run stored, for the tree `tree`), `holder` (`none` = no key holder runs yet: offline, unregistered), `arrives` (a secret that lands AFTER the first frame, or null), the `body` shown, `firstFrame` = the status of the first render, `after` = the status once `arrives` landed (same as firstFrame when nothing arrives).

staleTree.$comment: STALE TREE (#FEED-248, Danny's 'Couldn't send the message. The tree is at epoch 1' from a web tab whose synced sessions missed his conversation with an agent): the writer's synced store is a CACHE of the tree, never its authority. A send to an agent or an app (`agentId` / `appId`, no session id) whose conversation root the store does not have ASKS the server first (`sessions.sendTarget {agentId|appId}` -> {rootId, epoch, publicKey}) and only carries an inline `seal` (epoch 1) when the server names no root; a root the server names keyed is sealed to the server's key; a keyless one is keyed with `sessionKeys.create` first. A keyless root in the store whose `create` is refused asks `sessionKeys.publicKeys` before it falls back to plaintext. The server refuses a key write for a tree that moved on (an inline `seal` or a `create` whose epoch is not the next one) with CONFLICT and exactly `refusal`; a writer that gets it RESOLVES the tree again from the server (sendTarget / publicKeys, never the store), re-seals and re-sends ONCE by itself (no toast); a second refusal surfaces `refusal` as the failed send's description, never a raw epoch. Each case: `send` (`agent` = {agentId}, `session` = {sessionId} of a root), `local` (what the store has: `missing` | `keyless` | `keyed`), `server` (the tree on the server: `none` | `keyless` | `keyed`), `asks` (the server calls the writer makes before its first send, in order), `wire` (`inline` = seal epoch 1 rides along, `sealed` = text sealed to the server's current key, `create` = sessionKeys.create then sealed). `retryCases`: `refusals` = how many sends the server refuses with `refusal`; `sends` = how many sends leave; `outcome` = `sent` | `failed` (with `refusal` as the description).
staleTree.refusal: This chat's encryption key changed. Try again in a moment.

clearTree.$comment: #EDE-97 SEALED BY DEFAULT (design: #EDE-94's 'Session encryption: the dataflows today'). EVERY chat tree is sealed, except one kind: a ROOT an OUTSIDE MCP client starts (an MCP call with no calling session, i.e. not through a device's gateway, that carries no `seal`) is stamped `sessions.clear_tree = true` (SYNCED, roots only, never changes) and stays in clear FOR LIFE, so that client keeps sending into it and reading it: nobody keys it (`sessionKeys.create` and an inline `seal` for it are refused with `clearRefusal`; the device does not key it at its claim), every writer sends plaintext into it, its agent's cards and replies go plaintext. Old trees in clear (no key, `clear_tree` false) are left as they are; the first writer that holds a key keys them from then on. Lines the server writes itself (system cards, check and watch lines, trigger lines, bus fallbacks) and the routing metadata (`issue_brief`, mention / attachment / ref ids, card clear fields, the neutral `title`) stay clear as before. START (`startCases`, the server): `via` = `mcpOutside` (an MCP client outside any session), `mcpSession` (an agent through its device's gateway), `trpc` (a person's app), `server` (a trigger or schedule firing, an app hand-off, a suggestion started); `seal` = an inline key rides the start; `clearTree` = what the new root is stamped. WRITERS (`writerCases`, the pure `sendWire` of every writer x4: web seal-send.ts, iOS SendSealing.swift, Android SealedWriter.kt, Rust coding sealing.rs + the device gateway): NO SILENT PLAINTEXT. `tree` = where the text goes: `clear` (a clear_tree root), `new` (the send creates the root), `keyed`, `keyless` (an existing root without a key); `holder` = this process's key holder: `ready`, `late` (not running yet, it comes up within `holderWaitMs`: the writer waits for it, registering its install when it has none), `none` (none within the wait: signed out, eNet off, registration refused); `reader` = this install may key that keyless tree; `keyArrives` = a keyless tree this install may not key gets its key from its device's claim within `keyWaitMs`. `wire`: `plain` (only into a clear tree), `inline` (a new root's key rides as `seal`), `create` (`sessionKeys.create` first), `sealed` (the tree's current key), `failed` = nothing leaves: the send fails with the failed-action toast (feedback-states.json `errors`: `Couldn't send the message`, the description `noKeyRefusal`), the draft stays. An attachment-only send has no text and is not sealed (unchanged). CLAIM (`claimCases`, the device's pick-up, Rust pickup.rs): a root it claims without a key is keyed at once (`keys`) unless `clear_tree`; then, the tree keyed and not clear, the device RE-SEALS the session's first message (`reseals`) when it is still plaintext (the server wrote it before any key existed: a trigger or schedule firing, an app hand-off, a suggestion started, a raw tRPC start): it asks `sessions.resealTarget {sessionId, deviceId}` -> {messageId, body} | null and posts `sessions.reseal {sessionId, deviceId, messageId, body}` with the body sealed to the tree's current key. RESEAL (`resealCases`, the server): accepted ONLY when the caller is the device executing the message's session (`deviceId` = the session's), the tree is keyed and not clear, the message is that session's FIRST message (author user or agent), its stored body is plaintext (so the rewrite happens once), no agent reply follows it in that session yet, and the new body is a valid envelope at the tree's current epoch; the stored body is REPLACED (mentions, attachment and ref ids, `issue_brief` and the card stay); anything else is refused (`accepted: false`). CARDS (`cardCases`, plan.ts): a plaintext plan, question or show card into a KEYED tree is refused like a plaintext send (EXP-1472's `assertNotPlainInSealedTree`, its writer hint); a keyless or clear tree takes it; a sealed card goes as before. #EXP-2118: a plaintext suggestions / replies card (`kind`) is refused there too, nothing of a refused card stored. AGENT ROUTE (#EXP-2118): a session's agent reaches the MCP ALWAYS through its device's gateway, also when it is launched or revived before the device's key holder runs or is expected (its route is for life); the gateway decides per call by WRITERS (a late holder is waited for, none = the call fails and nothing leaves). A device whose gateway cannot start runs only sessions of a clear tree. MINIMUM VERSION: devices below `deviceMinVersion` (desktop and CLI) never key a tree: the server's CLIENT_MIN_VERSION gate holds them at that floor (a configured minimum below it counts as the floor). KEYLESS (#EXP-1960, `keylessCases`, the pure `keylessStep` of every writer x4): an existing keyless tree is keyed with `sessionKeys.create`; when that fails the writer reads the failure (`failure`) and takes a `step`, NEVER a silent wait: `clear` (`clearRefusal`) -> `plain`; `stale` (CONFLICT: keyed meanwhile) -> `serverKey` (its current key; none = `requestKey`); `notReader` (NOT_FOUND: this install may not key the tree, e.g. a pre-#EDE-97 chat of a teammate's device) -> `requestKey`; `wrapRefused` (`wrapRefusal`: a wrap names an install that is not a reader) -> `retryOwn` (create again wrapped for this account's own installs only; `ownOnly` = that retry was made, a second one -> `requestKey`); `refused` (any other 4xx) -> `failed`; `transient` (no answer, a 5xx, a timeout, a 429) -> `retry` (the same create after `createRetryMs` x `attempt`) while `attempt` < `createAttempts`, then `failed`. REQUEST KEY (`requestKeyCases`, the server `sessionKeys.requestKey {rootId}`): an idle chat's device claims nothing, so a keyless tree whose writer may not key it asks its DEVICE: the caller must see the root (a member of its team and the root `shared` or theirs, or the host of a device in the tree; else NOT_FOUND, like a missing root); a keyed root answers `keyed` {epoch, publicKey}, a clear one `clear`, a keyless one queues ONE `tree_key {rootId}` device command on every host devices row of the tree (lib/sessions/host.ts; a pending one is reused, `queued` = rows inserted) and nudges each device: `requested`; no host row: `noHost`. The writer then (`answer`): `keyed` -> `sealed`; `clear` -> `plain`; `requested` -> `wait` (the key polled for `keyWaitMs`, then `failed`); `noHost` -> `failed` at once; `notFound` (a real NOT_FOUND) and `error` (no answer, an older server) -> `wait` (the bare wait of before). The DEVICE (desktop app + CLI daemon) runs `tree_key` like its claim's key step (Rust `ensure_tree_key`: a no-op on a keyed or clear tree, never waits for its key holder) and completes the command; an app too old for the kind reports it unsupported and the writer's wait fails.

serverComposed.$comment: #EXP-1957 SERVER-COMPOSED LINES (the server half; replayed by apps/web server-composed.real-db.test.ts): a keyed tree refuses plaintext from every WRITER (`PLAIN_IN_SEALED_TREE_MESSAGE`), but text the SERVER composes from data it already holds in clear is a server line, legal plaintext there, like the bare issue-forward line: a reply chip or a suggestion's Do it here / Start of an UNSEALED card (the item text is clear on the card), an app's hand-off brief to a team agent (the package's prompt + the input as a data block), the `Link #A #B` wake line of a manual link. Only server code marks a send server-composed (`SendExtras.serverComposed`), never a tRPC or MCP input: the same text sent by a client or an MCP caller into the same keyed tree is still refused. A SEALED card stays refused (`SEALED_SUGGESTIONS_MESSAGE`): its items are not the server's to read; the client sends them sealed (`cardStamps`, #EXP-1958). `via` = the path, `card` = the card's state where one is acted on, `landed` = the plaintext line is posted (and the card item stamped).

cardStamps.$comment: #EXP-1958 SEALED REPLIES / SUGGESTIONS CARDS (the client half): the server never reads a sealed card's items, so a tap is the CLIENT's: it opens the card with the tree key and sends the picked item's text SEALED through the composer's own writer (`sessions.send`); the server only STAMPS the item, in that send's transaction, never seeing any text. STAMPS: a sealed `replies` / `suggestions` card carries the clear, server-written `stamps` = {<itemId>: stamp}; a stamp holds only `fields` (`sent`, `here`, `dismissed` = true; `sessionId`, `issueId` = a string id). Writers never send `stamps` (a writer's sealed card with it is refused like any non-clear field). `openCard` (status opened) lays each item's stamp over that item (the allowed fields only, of their type; a stamp for an id no item carries is ignored) and drops `stamps` from the opened card; any other status returns the clear part (stamps included) alone; a plain card is returned as is. So every reader shows a stamped item like a clear card's handled one (sent, started, here, filed, dismissed). `openCases`: `stored` = a `card.splits` name whose envelope gets `stamps`, opened with `keys` (`tree` | `none`) to `status` and the opened `items` (or, unopened, the clear `card`). WIRE (`tapCases`, `cardItemWire({stored, opened, action})` -> `wire` + `call`): an UNSEALED card keeps the server actions (`wire: server`: sendReply, startSuggestion child|here, startAllSuggestions, dismissSuggestion, dismissReplies, fileSuggestion; the server composes the text, #EXP-1957). A SEALED card this install OPENED (`wire: sealed`, `call: sessions.send` through the sealing writer, `cardItem: {messageId, itemId}` beside it): reply = `{sessionId: the card's session, text: the reply}`; Do it here = `{sessionId: the card's session, text: the item's request (title, a blank line, text)}`; Start = `{parentId: the card's session, text: the request, name: the title (leaves as sealedName), issueIds: the item's issue ids (uuids as they are, an #IDENT the client's issue store resolves, unknown dropped), deviceId / account / model as picked}`; Start all = Start for each open item in card order, one send each. The other actions stamp (`wire: stamp`): dismiss = `sessions.dismissSuggestion {messageId, itemId}`; dismiss replies = `sessions.dismissReplies {messageId, itemIds: every open reply}`; File as issue = `sessions.fileSuggestion {messageId, itemId, title, text}` (an issue is clear by design: the person publishes the item to the board; DECIDED 2026-11-19: it stays ONE tap, no warning and no confirm before it). A sealed card this install cannot open = `refused`: nothing leaves (the action toasts like a failed one). NEVER IN CLEAR: a `wire: sealed` tap hands OPENED text to the writer, so the tap path sends only what the writer SEALED: a prepared text that is no `exp-sealed:` envelope (the writer found a `clearTree` target, or has no sealer / keys) is refused locally like a failed action, before any request; no opened word leaves in clear, not even towards a server that would refuse it. An item the opened card no longer carries (`wire: sealed` | `stamp`) fails the same way, never a silent success. `cardItem` is tRPC only, never on the MCP tool. SERVER (`serverCases`, replayed by apps/web sealed-card-taps.real-db.test.ts on a tree started in clear, then keyed): a send with `cardItem` needs a SEALED replies / suggestions card the caller may steer (`loadSessionForUser` + `assertCanSteer` on the card's session: a session the caller cannot see is NOT_FOUND), a target that is the card's session (`sessionId`; on a suggestions card `parentId` too = Start; a replies card takes no Start), a SEALED text (`exp-sealed:`), and an item with no stamp yet (else CONFLICT and the send rolls back, nothing posted); the stamp (`sent` on replies, `here` on a message into the suggestions card's session, `sessionId` = the started child) is written under the message row's lock in the send's transaction. On a sealed card `sendReply`, `startSuggestion` and `startAllSuggestions` stay refused (`SEALED_SUGGESTIONS_MESSAGE`); `dismissSuggestion` stamps `dismissed`, `dismissReplies` stamps `sent` on each named id (no ids = BAD_REQUEST), `fileSuggestion` needs `title` + `text` (else BAD_REQUEST) and stamps `issueId`. BOUNDED: the server cannot tell which ids a sealed card carries, so every stamping path (the send's `cardItem`, `dismissSuggestion`, `dismissReplies`, `fileSuggestion`) takes only a uuid as item id (the writers mint uuid v4; anything else, `__proto__` included, = BAD_REQUEST and nothing is posted, stamped or filed) and refuses a NEW id once `stamps` holds as many entries as the card's kind has items at most (REPLIES_MAX on replies, SUGGESTIONS_MAX on suggestions; BAD_REQUEST); an id already in `stamps` is still stamped (dismissReplies) or a CONFLICT. `stamp` = what lands in `stamps[itemId]`, `landed` = the send / stamp happened, `code` = the refusal.

rotation.$comment: ROTATION (#EXP-1951, on #FEED-177's path): a tree's key ROTATES when a reader is DROPPED, so what is sealed afterwards is closed to a reader that kept the old secret (a lost or sold device, a copied keyring file, a removed member). THE SERVER (`dropCases`, lib/sessions/tree-keys.ts `dropNonReaderKeysInTx`) never sees a secret and cannot rotate: in the SAME transaction as the drop it deletes every `session_keys` row of the affected trees whose install is no longer a reader (so `mine` has nothing to hand that install, and `pending`, readers only, never names it again) and, on each keyed root that lost a row, sets `sessions.seal_rotate_epoch` = its current `seal_epoch` (the root is DUE; `create` clears it). The affected trees are the ones in which the dropped installs hold a wrap (an install without a wrap never had the secret); a member with thousands of trees costs a fixed number of queries per 500 roots, never some per root. `event`: `installRevoked` (`installs.revoke`), `memberRemoved` / `memberLeft` (`teamMembers.remove`, by an owner or by the member; their shares of the team end with it), `accountDeleted` (`users.deleteAccount`, `admin.deleteUser`: the installs cascade away, the roots are flagged first), `deviceUnshared` (`devices.setShared`, a team owner's or an admin's `dropShare`, a cleared squat: the installs of that devices row stop reading as the executing device), `deviceRemoved` (`devices.remove`), `shareDropped` and `hostRemoved` (the same rules, named for their case), `treePrivate` (#FEED-177: `shared` true -> false). THE WORLD of `dropCases`: one team, its owner the `starter` (`starterPhone`), a member `mate` (`mateBrowser`) and a member `host` whose server machine is shared into the team (`hostDaemon`, bound to that devices row, and `hostPhone`); the starter's chat runs on the host's machine and every install holds epoch 1 of what it reads. `tree`: `shared` (read by all four) or `private` (read by `starterPhone` and, as the executing device, `hostDaemon`). `event` acts on: `installRevoked` the starter's phone; `memberRemoved` / `memberLeft` / `accountDeleted` the mate; `hostRemoved` the host leaving the team; `deviceUnshared` (by its owner) / `shareDropped` (by the team's owner) / `deviceRemoved` the host's machine. `drops` = whose wraps go (the others keep theirs), `due` = the root is flagged. What a dropped reader could ALREADY read stays readable to it (old epochs are never re-sealed). WHO ROTATES (`rotatorCases`, `sessionKeys.create {epoch: seal_epoch + 1}`): the root's starter or an install of the executing device, at any time; while the root is DUE, ANY reader (the next holder that is online: the starter may be the member who was removed, and a shared chat must not wait for one device). Never a non-reader (NOT_FOUND), and every wrap of a create names a CURRENT reader (`clearTree.wrapRefusal` otherwise). THE HOLDER x4 (`stepCases` + `answerCases` = the pure `rotationEpoch` and `rotationAfter`; `holderCases` = one holder pass against a server double): every holder pass is `mine`, then the rotations, then `pending`. A root is rotated when it is flagged at the epoch this install knows as current, this install HOLDS that epoch's secret, and the server did not refuse it this (root, epoch) before (`left`). The due roots come from the synced root rows on the desktop app and the CLI daemon (`seal_rotate_epoch`), and from `sessionKeys.due {installId, limit<=200}` -> [{rootId, epoch}] on web, iOS and Android (the flagged roots whose current epoch this install holds a wrap of and still reads). The rotation is `sessionKeys.create {epoch + 1}` with a FRESH key and ONE wrap, this install's own; the other CURRENT readers get theirs from `pending`, which the server computes from the readers, so the holder never wraps the new epoch for an install the reader list no longer names (it wraps exactly the pairs `pending` lists). The answer (`answerCases`, `failure` = `createFailure` of the create, null = created): `adopt` (hold the new secret, answer `pending` at once), `reread` (`stale`: another holder rotated first; `mine` for that root, theirs is current), `leave` (`notReader`, `refused`, `wrapRefused`, `clear`: not this install's to rotate; remembered for this (root, epoch), never asked again), `retry` (`transient`: the same root on the next pass). `holderCases`: the holder is `install` (`self`); `held` = the epochs it holds per root before the pass (`tree.secret` at 1, `rotatedTree.secret` at 2); `due` = what the server names as due (it stops naming a root once a create for it was accepted or answered CONFLICT); `create` = the server's answers to the creates, in order (`ok`, a tRPC code, `blip` = no answer; `ok` when the list is used up); `readers` = the installs `pending` names for the new epoch after an accepted create; `serves` = `foreign`: the double's `mine` ALSO hands out `foreignWrap`, a row wrapped for another install (a server that keeps serving a dropped install's rows): it does not open and is never held; on CONFLICT `mine` serves `rotatedWrap` (the other holder's key, `rotatedTree`, wrapped for `install`) at the next epoch; `passes` (default 1). Expected: `creates` (every create sent, `wraps` = the installs it wraps for), `wraps` (every pair sent to `sessionKeys.wrap`), `holds` (the epochs held after the last pass). OLDER BUILDS: a holder that cannot rotate leaves the flag to one that can and follows the new epoch like any reader (`mine`); writers keep sealing to the key the root row names. Calls refuse a root that is due (`sessions.sendTarget` `rotationDue`, #EXP-1941).
